A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IFAdapter study, with readable text, equations, figures and tables across all 15 pages. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, despite both referring to one in Section 4.1.

before.justification: v1 reports original COCO IFG evaluations, a human evaluation study, token ablations and generated-image examples (Tables 1–3 and Figures 1–5).

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark evaluations, human study, ablations and generated examples, with updated full-model scores in Tables 1 and 3.

M1.justification: The appearance-token, instance-semantic-map and gated-fusion architecture and training procedure remain unchanged. Figure 2(b) already shows image features and EoT-plus-appearance tokens in v1; the revised Equation (5) aligns its formalization with that existing design.

E1.justification: Both retain COCO2014 and LAION5B training data, COCO IFG evaluation, COCO2017 references for FID, and the same multi-instance and community-model demonstrations. No dataset or evaluated task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains InstanceDiffusion, GLIGEN, MIGC, MultiDiffusion and DenseDiffusion. The user study in Table 2 retains InstanceDiffusion, GLIGEN and MIGC; comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the same SDXL training and inference settings, 1,000-image validation protocol, IFS/AP/CLIP/FID metrics and human-study design. No revised experimental setting accompanies the updated scores.

E4.justification: Section 4.6 still tests removal of appearance tokens and EoT tokens. The ablated variants' scores and Figure 5 examples are unchanged; only the full-model reference scores are updated.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v3 adds no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 3 revise full IFAdapter's QwenVL/InternVL/CogVL IFS rates from 75.8/66.5/58.8 to 79.7/68.6/61.0, AP from 48.3 to 49.0, and CLIP from 25.0 to 25.1. FID remains 22.0. Baseline and ablated-variant scores, user-study results, rankings and qualitative examples remain unchanged; the reason for the numerical revisions is not stated.

T1.justification: Equation (5) changes s_i = Attention(H_i, K, V, m_i) to s_i = Attention(Q, K_i, V_i, m_i). This corrects the formal semantic-map construction to use image-latent queries and instance-specific token keys and values. Other equations and mathematical definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: introducing IFG and its benchmark, improving instance-feature generation through IFAdapter, outperforming baselines, and supporting community models without retraining.

C2.justification: The explanations linking detailed annotations and appearance tokens to feature fidelity, semantic maps to spatial accuracy, and adapter design to image quality are retained. The qualification about VLM evaluation differing from human perception is also unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.3.2 now explicitly specifies that keys and values are projected from concatenated appearance and EoT tokens, while queries come from image latents. This refines implementation documentation; training hyperparameters, data annotation instructions, inference settings and project-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work section and reference list are unchanged. Introductory rewrites retain the same substantive positioning against existing layout-to-image methods and their limitations in generating detailed instance features.

P1.justification: The opening introduction receives localized rewrites, including changes from instances to objects and fashion-design to art-design examples. Equation explanations and two captions are edited, while section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 5 and Table 3 receive more descriptive, bold captions identifying qualitative and quantitative IFAdapter-variant results. The equation explanation causes minor reflow across pages 5–6. Figure content, table structures and their placement otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revised Equation (5) and explicit attention-input definitions resolve a local inconsistency with Figure 2, improving technical accuracy and reproducibility. The benefit is limited: the empirical evidence and conclusions largely persist, and the unexplained score increases without uncertainty estimates do not independently establish stronger evidence.
